name: NGC 4191 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4191, a slowly rotating early-type galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc4191-hubble
story: NGC 4191 hides two stellar components that rotate in opposite directions, a pattern astronomers suggest was built by gas falling in along two cosmic filaments. Hubble's sharp view of its center helps trace how such galaxies were assembled.

claims.text: NGC 4191 is one of the 12 slowly rotating early-type galaxies (ATLAS3D slow rotators) imaged by HST program GO-13324
NGC 4191 was targeted as a low angular momentum early-type galaxy
Gas accretion along two filaments is suggested as the formation mechanism of the counter-rotating components
NGC 4191 is classified as a 2σ galaxy (two off-center peaks in velocity dispersion)
